title: Night shift: sloth bear
storyboard: Film: our night camera-trap clip of a sloth bear at a termite mound, IR, 10–15 s

scenes.headline: A sloth bear on the night shift
scenes.body: Sloth bears may be active at night, by day, or at dawn and dusk.

scenes.headline: It came for termites
scenes.body: Sloth bears mainly eat termites and ants, sucking them up through a gap in their front teeth.

scenes.headline: Why a camera, not a torch?
scenes.body: A camera trap can watch all night without disturbing the bear.

caption:
The termite mound looked different in the morning. The camera knew why.

Sloth bears can keep a night, day or dawn-and-dusk schedule, so a camera that never sleeps is the fairest way to find them.

Source: Smithsonian's National Zoo, sloth bear. Photos/video: Wikimedia Commons (credits on screen).
notes: Storyboard: daytime CC photos stand in for our IR camera-trap clip; text is written as the real reel. Original: 'what dug here?' mystery solved by the trap.
